pages.scan: Opened works/auto-6294ee8a2094/workflow/review/page-02.png with Read and looked at the lettered art. The page has four panels. Panel A, full-width top tier: the doctor types on a laptop showing an onboarding form with step dots, in sunset light. A caption at top centre reads 'The clinic begins its Welbuk onboarding.' and a teal label at top right reads 'WELBUK PRACTICE for the clinic'. Panel B, middle left: the doctor, now with a stethoscope, sits at the laptop with a finger on her chin. 'We can organise our clinic workflow here.' has a tail to her head. Panel C, middle right: the receptionist in the blue kurta smiles and holds up a phone showing a calendar app. 'And our team can use tools suited to each staff role.' has a tail to her. At the bottom is a teal label 'WELBUK CARE for clinic staff'. Panel D, full-width bottom tier: the doctor sits at her desk raising a fist with a smile, and the receptionist stands at right holding her phone. 'One team. Better coordination.' has a short tail to the doctor's mouth. Reading order: caption, WELBUK PRACTICE label, doctor 'We can organise...', receptionist 'And our team...', WELBUK CARE label, doctor 'One team...'.
pages.observation: The order is clear and the tails are correct. In Panel D the tail is short but sits right at the doctor's mouth, and her raised fist fits the line. In Panel C the WELBUK CARE label covers the receptionist's lower dress near her left hand but not her face or the phone. The Panel A caption sits on the top border and the label touches the right border. The doctor has no stethoscope in Panel A but wears one in Panels B and D, a small continuity point. The PRACTICE and CARE labels read as product names but do not explain how the two differ beyond 'for the clinic' and 'for clinic staff'. All text is readable.
